title: Place answers against scored anchors
statement: Where a model's absolute marks drift, have it place each answer against human-scored anchor answers bracketing each score boundary, since models judge relative quality more stably than absolute scores.
detail: A grade 4-5 writing module's marker spec makes comparison with anchors its primary scoring mode wherever absolute scores drift: the answer is placed beside human-scored anchor answers on the same skill and passage, bracketing each band cut, and the model is asked whether it is stronger or weaker, never for a raw mark. An assessment BrainLift, citing a published benchmark of model judges, holds that models can be inconsistent on absolute ratings but are more stable on A-versus-B choices, especially with side-swapping and several votes.
against: The module has not measured it yet, and its harness makes no certification claim until a real gold set replaces the synthetic seed (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g4g5-writing/approval-package/sources/CALIBRATION-HARNESS-SPEC.md`, lines 122-123).

evidence.quote: place the response *beside* human-scored anchor exemplars (same KC, same anchor passage, bracketing each band cut) and ask stronger/weaker-than-X. Never an absolute 0/1/2 from the raw LLM.

Relative judgements reduce calibration problems. LLMs can be inconsistent on absolute 1–6 ratings but are more stable on “A vs B,” especially with side-swapping and multi-vote aggregation (arena/tournament style).

citations.ref: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena (NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks)
